doc.title: David Murray interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 18, 2003

title: The origin of 'Morning Song'
summary: The tune comes from his mother practicing at the piano in the morning after his father left for work.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Let me play — we had talked about this particular song, in the eighties.
Can you tell me where this particular song came from, or do you get your inspiration from any particular place?

I call that song “Morning Song” because it was a song that I heard my mother play. My father was a garbageman. And a lot of nights he would kneel down to pray, he’d go to bed fairly late to be getting up at 5:00. Sometimes I’d see him on his knees, I’d go to the bathroom late at night and he would actually be asleep in the middle of his prayers. And then it’s 5:00 and I know he had to get up right off his knees and go to work. And my mother would get up and try to get him out of the house, and as soon as she got him out of the house that was her quiet time, and this was the time that she would practice. And this is what I heard in this time. That’s why I call it “Morning Song.” Because it’s the music that I heard in the morning. Every morning I heard this.
And it sounds like even the same song or something. It was like a recurring thing she used to do, and to me it sounds like that. And she would sing too.
